newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila power firm needs 244 bln pesos over 10 yrs.
newsitem.headline: Manila power firm needs 244 bln pesos over 10 yrs.

text.p: The Philippines' state-owned National Power Corp (Napocor) said on Tuesday it needs about 244 billion pesos over the next 10 years to meet the growing demand for electricity.
"To install the needed capacity, Napocor needs about 244 billion pesos or approximately $8 billion for the period 1997 to 2006," Napocor said in a statement.
Napocor said 18 billion pesos were needed to build new power generation projects and 87 billion pesos for the construction and upgrading of transmission equipment.

A further 74 billion pesos would be used to maintain the existing generation and transmission facilities and 56 billion pesos for interest payments, subsidies for small electrification project and engineering support studies.
The rest of the budget had been earmarked for other expenses.

"The government is not in a position to raise the necessary funds to support the capital investment requirement. It has, therefore, become imperative to solicit the active involvement of the private sector in power generation and transmission to free the government of this heavy burden," Napocor added. ($1 = 30.1 pesos)
